title: A Go dependent's require follows the library, and stays isolated

setupFiles.monochange.toml:
[defaults]
parent_bump = "patch"

[package.core]
path = "core"
type = "go"
tag = true
version_format = "namespaced"
initial_version = "1.2.0"

[package.service]
path = "service"
type = "go"
tag = true
version_format = "namespaced"
initial_version = "1.0.0"

[ecosystems.go]
enabled = true
setupFiles..changeset/add-helper.md:
---
core: minor
---

Add a document helper
setupFiles.service/go.mod:
module github.com/acme/service

go 1.22

require (
	github.com/acme/core v1.2.0
	github.com/other/core v0.9.0
)

replace github.com/acme/core => ../core

setupCommands: git init -b main -q && git add -A && git commit -S -qm init && git tag core/v1.2.0 && git tag service/v1.0.0
expectation: Go modules carry no package version in go.mod. With tag = true, release planning resolves each baseline from a tag matching that owner's version_format; initial_version is a fallback only when no matching tag exists. This fixture already has core/v1.2.0 and service/v1.0.0 tags, so their baselines do not depend on initial_version. A minor change to core moves it to 1.3.0, propagates a patch to service, and rewrites its internal require directive to the newly released core version. replace directives are untouched, and github.com/other/core is not mistaken for the workspace module because dependency rewriting resolves full module paths. Supplemental isolated fixtures also verify custom tag formats, unrelated primary-tag exclusion, and complete dev prerelease suffix parsing.

checks.why: Parsing a Go release tag must preserve the whole dev prerelease version rather than splitting at the last v and silently falling back to initial_version.

checks.command: monochange preview --format json | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); t={x['id']: x['version'] for x in d['release_targets']}; assert t.get('core')=='1.3.0', t; assert t.get('service')=='1.0.1', t; print(t)"
checks.why: The existing owner-specific tags seed core at 1.2.0 and service at 1.0.0; initial_version is not required when those matching tags exist. The core minor and propagated service patch must both produce release targets.
Preparing the core 1.3.0 release must advance the service's internal require from 1.2.0 to the newly released version rather than leave its dependency reference stale.
The `replace` is a local development override. Rewriting it would break the workspace layout the repository depends on.
The ambiguity guard. Resolving by last path segment alone would rewrite an unrelated dependency to the workspace's version, silently corrupting a third-party pin.

checks.command:
git checkout -q service/go.mod; git checkout -q -- . 2>/dev/null; mkdir -p .changeset; printf -- '---
core: minor
---

Add a document helper
' > .changeset/grader.md; monochange prepare --format json > .p.json 2>&1; grep -q 'service/go.mod' .p.json; rc=$?; rm -f .p.json; test $rc -eq 0
checks.why: A rewrite that is not reported as a changed file would be invisible to the release commit and to review. The module file is restored and a fresh changeset written first, because an earlier check already ran `prepare`, which consumes changesets and rewrites the file in place.
Go has no manifest version field; pinning its absence stops a future change from inventing one that Go tooling would reject.
